findings.description: Remove-RetiredManagedRuntimeFiles validates only the lexical GetFullPath result and checks ReparsePoint only on the final item. If any ancestor below the runtime root is a symlink or junction to an external directory, the path still compares as under the root while Get-Item, hashing, and File.Delete follow that ancestor and operate on the external file. The editable previous marker supplies both managed_files.path and its expected hash, so a validly shaped marker can authorize deletion of a matching file outside the project. Resolve and contain every existing path component, or reject any reparse-point ancestor, before hashing or deleting.
findings.title: Retired runtime cleanup can delete a file outside the project

findings.description: Test-ContinuousCoReviewDigestPathDenied applies OrdinalIgnoreCase to every subtree prefix and IgnoreCase to every wildcard. On Linux or macOS, if canonical machinery such as .github/agents exists alongside a distinct reviewable path such as .GitHub/agents, the latter is removed from the temporary index even though Git treats it as separate source. The new exact ignored-path HashSet does not repair this downstream case-folding, so edits to omitted source can leave the reviewed tree identity unchanged. Use platform/Git-appropriate path identity and add a digest-level case-collision regression.
findings.title: Digest stripping still collapses distinct paths on case-sensitive hosts

findings.description: The host-mirror resolver omits .codex from hostDirs, and the generated .codex/agents files contain no .specrew-managed marker for the marker scan to discover. The frozen target therefore includes all five .codex/agents/*.toml files even though their headers identify them as Specrew-managed generated mirrors, while analogous host agent/skill mirrors are stripped. This violates the canonical machinery boundary and lets regenerated reviewer instructions perturb the certified source identity. Add the Codex host mirror to the single machinery policy with a paired reviewer-visibility regression.
findings.title: Generated Codex agents remain in the reviewed candidate

findings.description: testResults.xml is present in the target digest as an untracked generated Pester/NUnit report. Its environment and suite attributes disclose the origin working directory, machine/user identity, and absolute test paths. No repository ignore or runtime-classification rule excludes this output, so it violates the zero-origin-address reviewer-bundle requirement and makes candidate identity depend on stale machine-local test output. Ignore/classify this artifact or project sanitized evidence outside the reviewed source tree.
findings.title: Frozen candidate includes a machine-local test report with origin details

summary: Risk-based review completed. Both controller-declared verification commands succeeded on the exact target digest, but the candidate retains a destructive managed-runtime retirement path, two candidate-membership defects, and a machine-local test artifact in the reviewer-visible tree.
